The word "agha" entered English from Turkish, and the Turkish word comes from the Old Turkic "aqa," meaning "elder brother." It is an equivalent of the Mongolian word "aqa" or "aka." Other uses "Agha" is nowadays used as a common Persian honorific title for various individuals, such as a leader or a respected elder.

The word "Britain" comes from a Greek word, Πρεττανικη (Prettanike) or Βρεττανίαι (Brettaniai), used by Pytheas, an explorer. Previously in British English (but not in American English), the word "billion" referred exclusively to a million millions (1,000,000,000,000). However, this is not common anymore, and the word has been used to mean one thousand million (1,000,000,000).
